## What

`replication_soak` (5x kill/restart, both directions, 90s SLA) stayed RED in the
full live-federation gate long after EI-13317's "prompt forced-rejoin" fix
landed. The precise signature (frame `serve.log`):

- `[replication-liveness] repair-exhausted: forcing topic rejoin ... kind=connected_never_replicated` fired **promptly** (the boot.ts decision fix works — no 540s ladder wait).
- But the actual recovery — a live replicator re-attaching — took **341-378 seconds** after that decision, far past the 90s SLA.
- The `D-003` cgroup-v2 exclusive-cpuset frame isolation was confirmed ACTIVE, so it was **not** CPU-core starvation. And a live connection existed the whole time (`swarm has 1 live connection but this log has NEVER attached a replicator`), so it was **not** a DHT-discovery/rejoin-latency problem either.

If you see "forced rejoin fires but recovery takes minutes, and it isn't CPU or
DHT", this is almost certainly the shared-socket deadlock below.

## Why (root cause — a shared-socket eviction deadlock)

The substrate runs **one Hyperswarm** process-wide and joins many topics on it.
When two peers share a hive, ONE physical peer socket is **muxed across every
harness/topic they both belong to**. In the live-fed rig the same peer key
(`a6f76e39…`) carried `hello-world-pot` + `hello-world` + `papercusp` over a
single connection.

When the peer restarts, that shared socket can **half-open**: still live at the
transport layer (never fires its own `close`), but dead for replication — the
`connected_never_replicated` / WI-183 zombie class. Because it never closes,
`liveConnectionCount` never hits 0, so the severed-link tick (rung a) is blind to
it; instead the per-log detector fires `connected_never_replicated` for EVERY
harness muxed over that socket at once.

Each of those topics then runs `forceRejoinNow()`, whose only real lever for a
never-closing socket is to **destroy** it so Hyperswarm dials a fresh one. But
the eviction was guarded by `isSocketIdleAcrossAllTopics(socket)` — "only destroy
it if NO other harness/topic still claims it" (WI-5355's "never touch a socket
another join genuinely needs"). With the socket shared, that guard is **false for
every topic**: each one refuses to evict because the *others* still claim the
same dead socket. **Nobody evicts it.** The connection sits connected-but-dead
until the OS TCP keepalive/timeout finally closes it — ~6 minutes later — which
is the 341-378s recovery. The isolated `--only=replication_soak` run passed only
because it federated a single hive (no co-tenant harness to create the
deadlock); the full-suite gate has multiple harnesses on one socket, so it hit
it every run.

## The fix

A **forced** rejoin only happens after the repair ladder is exhausted — i.e.
this topic's link over the socket is already **proven dead**. A dead handshake is
dead for *every* topic muxed over the same physical socket (they all rode the one
connection). So `forceRejoinNow()` now **evicts unconditionally** — destroys the
socket even when another topic still claims it:

```ts
// swarm.ts forceRejoinNow() — was: if (isSocketIdleAcrossAllTopics(socket)) evict…
for (const socket of mySockets) {
  swarmJoinSocketTopics.get(socket)?.delete(topicHex); // unregister our claim
  evictIdleZombieSocket(socket);                        // destroy UNCONDITIONALLY
}
```

The `destroy()` fires the socket's own `close`; every sharing topic prunes its
bookkeeping and Hyperswarm redials a fresh connection that re-attaches
replication for all of them within seconds. The cost is a brief reconnect blip
for any co-tenant topic that happened to be genuinely healthy on the same peer —
bounded by the redial, and forced rejoin is a rare recovery action, so it is far
cheaper than a multi-minute federation freeze.

Regression test: `swarm.test.ts` "forceRejoin destroys a peer socket even when
another topic still shares it" — two topics on one swarm, one shared socket,
assert `forceRejoin()` destroys it (the pre-fix behavior left it alone).

## How to diagnose this class

1. In the frame `serve.log`, find `repair-exhausted: forcing topic rejoin` and
   measure the gap to the next successful merge/replicator-attach for that log.
   Minutes (not seconds) with the decision firing on time = recovery is blocked,
   not un-triggered.
2. Rule out the cheap causes first: confirm cpuset isolation was active (not CPU
   starvation) and that `swarm has N live connection(s)` is non-zero (not
   DHT-discovery latency — a live connection already exists).
3. The tell: the **same peer key** appears under **multiple harnesses** in the
   log (`peer_connected harness=X peer=P`, `harness=Y peer=P`, …) AND several of
   them report `connected_never_replicated` in the same window. That is one
   shared muxed socket dying for all of them → the eviction deadlock.

## Parallel candidate (not yet fixed)

`topic-gossip.ts` carries the **identical** `isSocketIdleAcrossAllTopics` guard
around its own forced-rejoin eviction (its `isSocketIdleAcrossAllTopics` +
`evictIdleZombieSocket` call). The presence/gossip channel over a shared socket
is subject to the same deadlock; apply the same "forced rejoin evicts
unconditionally" change there if presence-gossip recovery shows the same
minutes-long stall after a restart.
